pr_title: Add markers to edges rather than distributions
pr_body:
## Summary

We've debated this a bit but the thing that tipped me over the edge is https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/4157. As-is, there's no way to represent "a package should be installed, but the extra should only be installed conditionally based on the markers", because the markers sit on the _distribution_. By placing the markers on the edge, we can now represent scenarios that weren't previously representable.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/4137.
Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/4125.
Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/4157.
pr_comments: I think it's possible that we could continue to store markers on distributions _if_ we changed the schema such that extras were once again stored as their own "distributions" (i.e., their own nodes in the graph), and then changed the routine in `graph.rs` to treat a `None` marker as "universal" (right now, `None` markers are discarded, effectively).

issue_context.title: Setuptools is installed conditionally when it should be installed unconditionally
issue_context.body: Resolving this [pyproject.toml](https://gist.github.com/konstin/365b137c572a718e342b6635e49840fa) (needs minification) with `uv lock` on ubuntu, i get this [uv.lock](https://gist.github.com/konstin/90a99e5911e30b0cc90a681de71ca91a). If i `uv sync` it, it installs `pyramid`, but not setuptools, even though pyramid depends on setuptools. This does not happen if `pyramid` is the sole dependency.
comments: I can take this one later, unless someone beats me to it. Very weird, good bug!
I can't reproduce -- it does install setuptools for me.
Ah ok. You need to use Python < 3.12.

review_comments: Out of curiosity, why the change in Python version here?

I think it was because we typically test against 3.12 and 3.8. (This isn't required, it's just the common versions we use in these tests.) And so if I left it as-is, I would've had to install on 3.7 to hit the "exclusion" case. So it was just a bit easier to raise to 3.10, so that 3.12 is above and 3.8 is below.
Yeah, I think I buy this.
